author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page number below 1 as the first page
summary: Requesting the owner listing with a page number of 0 or any negative number shows the normal listing's first page instead of the error page. Bug fix; the owner's quoted expectation is the bar.
acceptance_criteria: given a page number of 0 or a negative number, when the owner listing is requested, then its first page is shown and marked as current, not an error page (HTTP 200 per the intake)
given a page number below 1 and a last name matching exactly one owner, when the search runs, then that owner's record opens directly, as it would for the first page
non_goals: page numbers past the last page
any change to page size or other listing behavior
notes: Intake line 1 carries no decisions beyond the request; scope is exactly the request text. The first test name is one data-driven test covering 0 and a negative value. Page numbers past the last page and non-numeric values are recorded as an Open Question in docs/prd.md, not decided. No Non-Goals row touched; no autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by docs/architecture-principles.md § Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the fix belongs in OwnerController and nowhere else. Root cause (grep basis, IDE oracle not connected): OwnerController.processFindForm passes the raw `page` request parameter to findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, which calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize); Spring Data rejects a negative page index with IllegalArgumentException, which renders the error page. Fix shape: clamp `page` to a minimum of 1 once, at the top of processFindForm, before both the repository query and addPaginationModel, so the first page is fetched AND reported as currentPage (AC 1) and the single-match redirect sees first-page results (AC 2). No domain, repository, or view change. docs/system-design.md § Contracts OwnerController row now lists REQ-OWN-005; no other design-doc write.
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch and request-parameter binding — the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

Repository (OwnerRepository): keep the existing @MockitoBean stub already wired in OwnerControllerTests (@WebMvcTest slice has no JPA context, so a real repository does not fit; a hand-written double would duplicate the existing fixture). Assert on the Pageable passed to findByLastNameStartingWith (page index 0) so the test proves the clamp, not just the 200.
Binding: no new entry point. The existing /owners GET binds `page` as a request-scoped int primitive and the Owner search probe under the existing @InitBinder disallow-list; unchanged.

patterns.description: Request-parameter normalization to its permitted range is binding, owned by the controller
Single normalization point feeding both the query and the currentPage model attribute

risks.risk: Clamping only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName would fix the 500 but leave currentPage reporting 0 or a negative number, failing AC 1's 'marked as current'.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at handler entry and use the normalized value for both calls (architecture-principles § Web controller).

risks.risk: Scope creep into page numbers past the last page or non-numeric values.
risks.mitigation: Out of scope per prd-entry non_goals and the PRD Open Question; do not touch them.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Owner listing path is already paged at a fixed page size; the slice adds no path that scales with data. docs/system-design.md carries no § Scale and Load section, so no row is cited — a gap for a later slice that adds a data-scaling path, not this one. VetController's pagination helper has the same PageRequest.of(page - 1, …) shape; it is not in this slice's scope and is not to be changed here.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Input validation: OwnerController.java processFindForm clamps the request-supplied page with `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, 1);` before `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)`, so page=0, negatives and Integer.MIN_VALUE no longer throw IllegalArgumentException. Before this change that exception went to the error page, which system-design.md:206 records as rendering exception text. The change therefore narrows exception-text exposure and adds no reach.
A non-numeric page still fails type conversion in the binder exactly as before. The PRD records it as an open question, and this change does not affect that behavior.

Binding surface unchanged: the diff adds no @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody target, and `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` at OwnerController.java:61 stays in place. The only new binding is the explicitly named @RequestParam `page`, an int.

No removed or weakened check: the diff deletes nothing except the old `processFindForm` signature line. The redirect target is still built from the persisted owner id, not from request text, so this adds no open-redirect path.

No secrets in the diff. It contains none of token/password/secret/key/credential, going by the full `python3 scripts/changeset.py` output read in this review. There is no logging, no file I/O, no shell execution and no template-expression change.

Pattern-consistency sweep: VetController.java:61 `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` has the same pre-existing unclamped page. This slice leaves it untouched and does not spread the weakness to a new path, so it is out of this slice's scope.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set, so dependencies are unchanged. Spring Boot plugin is 4.1.1 per build.gradle:5. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured and was not run, so no NVD match ran in this review.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner-listing page numbers below 1 to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production method in OwnerController, its controller test, and two doc lines that add the requirement and its traceability entry; no sensitive paths, one module.

semantic_surprise.note: Math.max(requestedPage, 1) runs before both the repository call and the currentPage model attribute, so page 1 and above behave exactly as before. The explicit name = "page" keeps the same request parameter, and Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps without overflow. Nothing is hidden behind the rename.
